title: How an Everyday Word in a Tool Schema Changes AI Agents' Searches While Every Call Stays Valid
description: An AI agent fills the fields of a tool with values from a fixed list, the tool's schema. Some allowed values are also everyday words. A traveller who asks for "a hotel" can mean any place to stay, but a booking tool can separate hotel from guesthouse. This preprint asks whether such a value name changes what an agent searches for while every call stays valid. It uses public MultiWOZ booking dialogues and nine language models. In 5.6% to 18.8% of valid first answers, depending on the model, the search would have excluded every place that fits the traveller's task. In tests registered before we opened the answers, a rename of the field and the value removed hotel filters that the task did not need, and also filters that it needed. The preprint also gives a release test for schema updates. It shows that the verdict on a repair depends on the reference record. The evidence concerns one word in one corpus.
